objective: Compress pendant star-coloring boundaries into exactly 306 labeled compatibility classes and derive a lossless minimum-old-edge-edit recurrence on subcubic trees.

atomic_claims.text: Exactly 306 pendant signatures are realizable, with 6, 60 and 240 signatures for zero, one and two nonunit coordinates.
Each pair of distinct labeled signatures is distinguished by a star-colored path exterior, and equal signatures have identical gluing compatibility.
The three rooted-tree conditions are necessary and sufficient and determine the output signature.
The stated dynamic recurrence computes the exact minimum number of changed old edges; the new leaf edge has zero edit cost.

assumptions: Finite simple subcubic graphs with the contract's proper star edge-coloring definition.
Pendant branches have one degree-one boundary vertex and share only that vertex with an exterior.
The edit recurrence is applied to a tree G rooted at the newly added leaf v and to the supplied old star coloring of G-v.
risks: The recurrence is restricted to trees; cycles cannot be silently discarded.
A boundary signature alone is not a cost vector.
Labels must not be independently quotiented away when reference costs are fixed.
The state-count minimality concerns compatibility information, not every possible algorithm.
No implementation, regression test, closure computation or kernel check was run.
